rundown: Argentina beat Italy 19-14 at Stadio Luigi Ferraris in Genova, Italy. Argentina led 19-14 at the half and held on.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 14, 6:36 AM ET. It had Argentina 71% and Italy 29%, projecting Argentina 32.1 – Italy 23 (55.1 total, Argentina by 9).

Final: Argentina 19 – Italy 14. Right winner: it had Argentina at 71%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Argentina came in with a 3% above average attack and a 20% leakier than average defense (LTLLL, 27.3 scored and 35.3 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 11 and 11 games of evidence. Projected to score 32.1, they scored 19 (−13.1 points, 41% under); projected to allow 23, they allowed 14 (−9 points, 39% under).

Italy came in with a 25% below average attack and a 42% leakier than average defense (LLLLL, 11 scored and 49.3 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 11 and 11 games of evidence. Projected to score 23, they scored 14 (−9 points, 39% under); projected to allow 32.1, they allowed 19 (−13.1 points, 41% under).

The bigger miss was Argentina's scoring (-13.1 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 33 against 55.1 projected (-22.1), about the 7th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15).

Margin: Argentina by 5 against Argentina by 9 projected, about the 60th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±16).

An unusual result, but one the simulations saw regularly (roughly one game in six to one in twenty).

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; there were no odds to check the projection against.

The result was off its normal range without being an outlier, so the flags may have played a part.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.603 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by +4 points. It counts toward Rugby scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
